originality.rationale: 2013 primary full-text and actual record searches compared by implication, not just titles. Banks–Martin sufficient inequality is algebraically the same as rank-one threshold for two primes and is credited; published weighted theorem t>1 does not contain an all-t>0 complete rank-optimizer formula, particularly the rank transitions below t*. Related k-primitive and finite-grid antichain sources were distinguished; equivalent unindexed weighted-poset theorems are a genuine risk.
residual_risks: The Banks–Martin finite-support proof technique may extend without substantive change from t>1 to positive t, potentially implying prime-layer optimality above the threshold; the additional exact subcritical all-optimizer theorem is the novelty focus.
Unindexed classical weighted Sperner/antichain literature might imply the same geometric-weight optimum without the number-theory wording.
The 2024 finite-antichain note abstract was accessible but its full text was not read.
Search coverage and a self-review do not certify publication priority or independent proof validation.
